exact_current_arithmetic.allocator: Alloc::take reserves round_up(payload + 256, 256) bytes for each take. bytes_needed is a count-only planner followed by 8 MiB loan slack; the GDN, QSA and MoE subplans are nested in one shared region sized to max(gdn_set_bytes, qsa_set_bytes, moe_set_bytes), not their sum.
exact_current_arithmetic.native16_layout: The current native16 carve has no native16-specific size plan. It overlays typed pointers onto the old allocations: R16 and gated_b16 occupy disjoint halves of the old T*D float gated allocation; lo_b16/bo_b16 and GU_b16/Dm_b16/sgate_b16/sup_b16/shared_b16 borrow old FP32 extents. The R float buffer remains used for the layer-1 PLE bridge and final FP32 callback. QSA is still FP32 unless its separate typed-QSA option is enabled.
exact_current_arithmetic.planner_mismatch: With scratch alias mode 0, bytes_needed manually counts an FP32 T*D xn take even when gr_unfused is false. carve/take_scratch_prefix omits xn in that case, and native16 layer-major rejects gr_unfused. At T=8192 this count-only excess is exactly 335544576 B (320 MiB payload plus the 256 B take guard); it is reservation slack, not evidence of an allocation actually made by init.
exact_current_arithmetic.illustrative_typed_extent: At T=8192, the current MoE Dm reservation is 8192*10*2560*4 = 838860800 B, while native16 writes/combines 2-byte Dm values spanning 419430400 B. This is a candidate extent difference only: the shared max-region may still be sized by QSA or GDN.

lifetime_and_correctness_constraints: Prefill::run keeps n<=m.T on run_impl; n>m.T selects run_layer_major. A smaller long arena must not invalidate the short FP32/decode-layout path in the same request owner or borrowed cache slots.

run_layer_major rejects m.T or m.T_max above 8192 and also gates geometry, full single-GPU topology, native source, compact FP16 MoE, explicit MMQ=0, same queue, observers and control-vector cases. Removing the 8192 checks alone does not establish other buffer, API, admission or kernel bounds.

PLE at layer 1 consumes an FP32 bridge and then repacks BF16 residuals; the final on_chunk16 restores FP32 before existing MTP/decode/NLL callbacks. Intermediate saved residuals are already two bytes per element under the BF16 plan.

Session GDN recurrent state, QSA indexer float tails/pools and PLE history remain FP32. The current GDN recurrence also writes both its FP32 y scratch and a 16-bit y16 output; making y optional would require a separate kernel/API review.

Preserve checked queue drains, callback/field restoration and live owners on failure, plus shared session state. Source arithmetic cannot qualify free-VRAM admission, runtime allocator behavior, speed, full-context correctness, RESTORE or numerical quality.
assessment.central_conclusion: There is a concrete unanswered source question: compare a long-only native16 layout with a temporally remapped shared arena and determine whether either can reduce actual owner/reservation bytes after accounting for the FP32 short path and the max-sized GDN/QSA/MoE region. Current source proves typed overlays and a planner overcount, not a safe reclaim amount or any chunk above 8192.
